record.paper: Typical and Extremal Aspects of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs

dossier_meta.paper: Typical and Extremal Aspects of Friends-and-Strangers Graphs
dossier_meta.statement_text: The threshold for $\mathrm{FS}(X, Y)$ to be connected when $X, Y \sim G(n,p)$ is determined by the isolated-vertex threshold: ``it seems that (as in the usual case of a binomial random graph) this local obstruction to connectedness tells essentially the whole story.''
dossier_meta.context_text: Theorem 1.1 establishes a lower bound $p \leq (2^{-1/2}-\varepsilon)/n^{1/2}$ arising from isolated vertices and an upper bound $p \geq \exp(2(\log n)^{2/3})/n^{1/2}$ for the high-probability connectivity threshold of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$. The authors suggest the gap between these bounds is an artifact of the proof method and that the two thresholds should coincide up to lower-order factors.
